args.message:
Fix round_money to use ROUND_HALF_EVEN (banker's rounding) per FIN-212

The nightly test expects 2.665 -> 2.66 (banker's rounding), but the
implementation used ROUND_HALF_UP. Switch to ROUND_HALF_EVEN.

args.body:
## Summary
`round_money` in `src/money.py` was using `ROUND_HALF_UP`, but per FIN-212 it must use banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`). This caused the nightly build to fail on `tests/test_money.py` (`2.665` should round to `2.66`, not `2.67`).

## Changes
- Switch `round_money` to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.

## Testing
- CI run `ci-0001` on commit `08d3cd5986` passed, including `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even`.
args.head: fix/round-half-even-fin212

transcript.content: I'll start by looking at the failing test and the current money implementation.
The fix is clear: `round_money` uses `ROUND_HALF_UP` but should use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. I'll create a branch and commit the fix.
transcript.reasoning_content:
The fix: change ROUND_HALF_UP to ROUND_HALF_EVEN. Check 2.675 → with ROUND_HALF_EVEN quantize on Decimal("2.675"): 2.675 is exactly representable in Decimal, half is 7 (odd) so rounds up to 2.68. 2.665: half digit 6 (even) rounds down to 2.66. Good.

Create branch, commit, run CI.
